value.rationale: PASS: The sign of quadrature weights decides positivity preservation and the absolute-weight condition number; sparse sensor failures are a natural axis beyond maximal displacement. The proof shows a sharp complexity transition between one and two displaced sites in the standard half-mesh model, an explicit finite-order sensitivity frontier and its asymptotic limit. It explains why failure of positivity need not entail substantial norm amplification, complementing broad negative-weight constructions that move many nodes. The threshold is neither artificially selected nor claimed universal across all two-node patterns.
